topic.source_contract: Ordnance Survey open location identifiers and relationships

facts.coverage: every addressable location in Great Britain
facts.scope_guard: A UPRN coordinate is an addressable-location reference and not a legal parcel, owner or HMLR title polygon.
Identifier relationships support data linkage and visualisation but do not establish ownership, legal boundary or planning entitlement.

facts.feature_relationships: properties, streets and OS MasterMap identifiers
facts.scope_guard: API capability is not evidence that a candidate-specific identifier query or relation was executed.
A TopographicArea or road relationship is mapping context and not a cadastral title, highway right or planning red-line.

facts.purpose: persistent identifiers for linking and tracking real-world locations/features
facts.scope_guard: Persistence of an identifier does not prove current use, ownership, permission or legal extent.

scope_guards: A UPRN is a persistent addressable-location identifier and not an HMLR title or legal parcel.
OS Open UPRN includes non-postal features, so UPRN existence is not proof of a dwelling or building.
UPRN coordinates are points and not surveyed or registered boundary vertices.
UPRN, USRN and TOID relationships support joining and visualisation rather than ownership or planning entitlement.
A TopographicArea TOID is not automatically the candidate site, application red-line or title polygon.
Road and street relationships do not establish a private right of access or public-highway legal extent.
Dataset/API availability and six-week updates do not prove execution of a candidate-specific join.
No score or promotion is written without exact identifier execution, HMLR title relation, current planning case and overlays.
